A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIDD study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original protein, DNA, and molecule generation experiments in Section 6 and Appendix E, including benchmark results and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds empirical comparisons, sensitivity analyses, value-estimation experiments, and reward-noise tests in Appendices E–G.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the mixed off-policy roll-in, lazy roll-out updates, and value-weighted forward-KL objective. The argmax implementation disclosure and Monte Carlo comparison expand documentation and analysis without establishing a change to the default VIDD procedure.

E1.justification: The protein SS-match, PD-L1/IFNAR2 binder, HepG2 enhancer, and Parp1 molecule-design coverage is retained. Appendix G adds binder training under synthetically corrupted reward signals, introducing a limited new training-environment scenario.

E2.justification: v3 Table 8 adds GLID2E and a KL-regularized DRAKES comparison for DNA generation. The earlier DRAKES numbers reappear as DRAKES w/o KL, so that row is retained under a more specific label. Protein and molecule comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds DNA log-likelihood and binder pTM/pDockQ evaluation, broader update-interval and regularization sweeps, a four-sample Monte Carlo comparison, and noisy-training/clean-evaluation controls. Table 4 also revises reported binder sequence length from 256 to 100. The PDFs do not establish whether that revision corrects documentation or reflects rerun experiments.

E4.justification: v2 already examined DNA update intervals, roll-in mixtures, and reward–diversity tradeoffs. v3 substantially extends sensitivity testing to protein update intervals and DNA/protein regularization, compares argmax-based and Monte Carlo value estimates, and tests reward-noise robustness in Appendices F–G.

E5.justification: Both retain median reporting and the same Table 1 caption describing ± as standard error with a 95% confidence interval. Additional estimates follow the existing practice; v3 supplies no new seed counts, repeated-run information, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Default VIDD benchmark values are retained, but DDPP protein results change: Table 1's β-sheet fraction changes from 0.60 to 0.63, pLDDT from 0.40 to 0.36, and diversity from 0.90 to 0.85. Binder DDPP rows and Figures 5–6 also change. Substantial new results cover added metrics and analyses; for example, v3 Table 23 reports PD-L1 reward 0.4744 at noise=0.1 versus 0.9079 without noise, under the newly tested conditions.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its Appendix A proof are retained. Appendix B removes v2's final reformulation that absorbs the value normalizer into the roll-in distribution, ending instead at the normalized objective in Equation 5. The additional conditional-KL expansion mainly explains the existing derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that iterative off-policy distillation enables diffusion fine-tuning for potentially non-differentiable rewards, with improved stability, sample efficiency, and biomolecular reward optimization. Removing a repeated PPO-comparison sentence does not materially alter these retained claims or the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of low DNA 3-mer correlation and explanations of the stability and computational tradeoffs among argmax, Monte Carlo, and learned value estimates. Appendices C.2 and G expand the limitations discussion to reward-exploitation tuning and the absence of explicit noise-robustness mechanisms, going beyond v2's general warning about imperfect rewards.

D1.justification: v3 maps the existing update-interval choices to individual protein tasks and newly discloses argmax decoding, temperature sampling for the alternative estimator, and generator/reward-model parameter counts. The abstract replaces the direct repository pointer with a project-page pointer. These are limited additions and revisions to reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Cao et al. (2025), Bryant et al. (2022), and Tang et al. (2025), supporting the additional baseline, pDockQ metric, and inference-time discussion. Appendix E.1 more explicitly distinguishes VIDD from the already cited SVDD. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the order of Sections 1–7 are retained. Changes include local wording and terminology corrections, expanded derivation explanations, new appendix subsections, updated publication/header text, and moving the generated-sample discussion from Appendix F to H.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation expands substantially through dedicated DNA-comparison, binder-metric, sensitivity, value-estimation, and noise tables. The retained DNA update-interval table gains log-likelihood and another interval, while Figures 5–6 show revised and extended DDPP traces. The document also adopts the ICLR layout and relocates retained displays.

improvement.justification: v2 provided limited direct evidence for the value-estimator choice and protein hyperparameter sensitivity. v3 tests these central design choices, expands DNA comparisons and unoptimized binder metrics, and quantifies the reward-noise failure previously discussed only generically. These additions substantially strengthen empirical support and clarify applicability boundaries, although the binder-length revision remains unreconciled with retained scores.
